answer: Because the pigment index resolves every citation against the lantern checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the haven audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 280 aliases as a result forfeits the authoring cost 280 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A farm of 3370 identities would post 4263 proofs and burn roughly 74 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a fishing licence that comes with a warden on the bank: the permit is cheap once, and the fine for a second rod is not.
